title: Water's Wild Ride
subject: science
instructions: Write your ID in the boxes at the top right, not your name. For multiple choice, circle one letter.

questions.prompt: Puddle Mystery: A puddle on the playground is gone by lunch on a sunny day. Where did the water go?

options.text: Into the air as water vapor
options.why: Yes: the sun's energy evaporated it into the air.

options.text: It was destroyed by the heat
options.why: Matter isn't destroyed. It became a gas you can't see.

options.text: Down to the center of the Earth
options.why: Some soaks in, but on a sunny day most rises as vapor.
Water vapor is still water, just as a gas.

questions.prompt: Cloud Factory: Which step of the water cycle forms clouds?

options.why: Evaporation lifts vapor up; clouds form when it cools.
Yes: vapor cools and condenses into tiny droplets.
Precipitation is water falling out of clouds.
Collection is water gathering in lakes and oceans.

questions.prompt: Sweaty Glass: On a hot day, drops of water form on the outside of a glass of ice-cold lemonade. Where do the drops come from?
questions.key: Water vapor in the air touches the cold glass, cools, and condenses into liquid drops. Full credit: the water comes from the air (water vapor) and cooling or condensing turns it into drops. Partial: names condensation but not where the water comes from, or says it comes from the air but not why it turns to drops. Incorrect: the lemonade leaks or seeps through the glass.

questions.prompt: State Changes: Label each arrow with the change it shows.

diagram.description: Three boxes in a row: Ice (solid), Water (liquid), Water vapor (gas). Arrow 1 points from ice to water, with label box 1 above it. Arrow 2 points from water to water vapor, with label box 2 above it. Arrow 3 points back from water vapor to water, with label box 3 below it.

questions.prompt: The Whole Cycle: Draw the water cycle with a lake or ocean, a cloud, and arrows. Label evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

diagram.description: An empty frame. Everything inside it was drawn by the student.

checklist.item: A body of water (a lake, ocean, or river) is drawn.
An arrow goes up from the water toward the sky or a cloud, labeled evaporation (any spelling).
A cloud is drawn, labeled condensation (any spelling) at or near the cloud.
Rain or snow is shown falling from the cloud, labeled precipitation (any spelling).
The water's path returns to the lake or ocean (an arrow, runoff, or rain landing in it), closing the loop.

questions.prompt: Mountain to Sea: How does rain on a mountain reach the ocean?
questions.key: Full credit names a path: it runs downhill over the ground into streams and rivers that flow to the ocean (runoff), or it soaks into the ground and flows underground (groundwater) to the ocean. Partial: says it flows or moves without saying how or where. Incorrect: it stays on the mountain or disappears.
